analysis:
All changes are in the PR threat-review CI tooling under .github/scripts. They do not touch the provider, coordinator contract, keys, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011, A-016) or inference paths. No canonical threat IDs (TB-002, TB-011, T-052..T-058) are affected, and I found no provider-side regression.

Changed behavior reviewed:
- bedrock.py adds a last_request diagnostic dict, request_id, stop_reason and latency_ms. It records these in the usage ledger and raises ReviewFailure with codes instead of ReviewUnavailable. Fallback is still limited to the UNAVAILABLE codes (bedrock.py:128-129). The call limit and no-fallback-around-limit behavior are unchanged (lines 83-86). Response validation is stricter: non-dict envelope, non-dict usage and bad text blocks all fail closed.
- threat-bedrock-smoke.py:53-58 prints json.dumps of failure_record to public CI logs and writes it to the ledger. threat-model-review.py:23-24 and budget_runner.py (about lines 177-192) call write_diagnostics. The new tests (test-threat-diagnostics.py) assert that private text and exception messages are excluded, and that request_id accepts only a UUID.
- budget_runner.py status_body now adds a human-review-required notice and a diagnostics code list. The override text now uses replace(old, new, 1) instead of rsplit, so if the old sentence is absent the clearance text is silently omitted. This is a minor wording-robustness issue, not a security regression.
- The smoke test and tests now propagate needs_deeper_review into integration, and the test asserts that uncertainty is preserved across multi-tier integration.

Coverage limit: threat_review/diagnostics.py (failure_record, parse_object, write_diagnostics, request_id), change_context.py and the review.py/budget_scan.py changes were not supplied. I could not verify that diagnostics output is free of private data, or the artifact path handling of THREAT_REVIEW_DIAGNOSTICS_FILE. The integration pass should check diagnostics.py for allow-list sanitization.
